card: Adds an -ipcconnect option to bitcoin-wallet and -ipcbind to bitcoin-node for multiprocess builds, establishing an IPC connection over a local socket to a running node. The bitcoin-wallet utility is currently offline-only and cannot sync or interact with an active node. This change provides the underlying IPC connection scaffold needed for future online commands like wallet sync and RPC serving. It depends on #10102 and #29409 and unblocks #19461.
changed_since_previous: Rebased onto updated base branches, pulling in libmultiprocess subtree updates to version 14, btcsignals eager destruction adjustments, and CI compatibility fixes.
evidence: PR description: 'The idea is that `bitcoin-wallet` can be extended in the future to have some online functionality. For example, there could be a `bitcoin-wallet sync` command... or a `bitcoin-wallet serve` subcommand...'

PR description: 'This PR is small and doesn't do much. The only visible change is that `bitcoin-wallet` now checks whether a node socket exists on startup and prints "Connected to IPC address" if it can connect to it.'
problem: The `bitcoin-wallet` tool operates strictly offline and cannot interact with a running node to inspect chain state, synchronize transaction history, or execute wallet RPCs.

risk.why: Affects only multiprocess builds behind compile-time flags; a failure would manifest as connection errors or crashes when running bitcoin-wallet with IPC enabled.

scope_notes: Part of the process separation project. The branch is stacked on #10102 and #29409, and includes an update to the `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree. The changes only take effect when building with multiprocess IPC enabled.
summary: Adds the `-ipcconnect` command-line option to `bitcoin-wallet` and `-ipcbind` to `bitcoin-node` in multiprocess builds. When enabled, `bitcoin-node` listens on a local domain socket and `bitcoin-wallet` connects to it upon startup, verifying the connection before proceeding with its command or falling back to offline mode.
